utterances.text: I am sorry, the document which you have shown to the witness is 1D141, and that is a footnote 71 in the expert report and it's at tab 27 of the announced documents for the Defence. Now, I didn't announce the document referred to in footnote 482 but I can try to provide that over the break for your reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, my question is -- do we have 1D141 on the screen? And I understand my learned friend to be saying that is the document listed in footnote 71 as Official Gazette HZ, Herceg-Bosna. If it's not, then either the Defence has identified the document incorrectly in e-court or the witness has the wrong reference in his footnote. I am sorry, Your Honours, in order to save time, let me move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, I want to talk about the Cutileiro Plan a little bit and Annex 9 of your report. Now, just to be clear because this term Cutileiro Plan has been thrown around a lot. And when you say Cutileiro Plan, can you indicate for us a specific document that you would be referring to when you say Cutileiro Plan?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably got all sources that I mentioned in the footnotes in electronic form. When we speak about the Cutileiro Plan, that's a process. Five or six meetings of the highest representatives of the three sides in Bosnia-Herzegovina under the auspices of the international community. That was a generally known fact in the world at the time. And any conclusions reached or agreements at those meetings are the ones I mention in those parts of my report where the context requires it. In Annex 11, there's just one of these documents that was made after a series of these meetings that mark the development of the political crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the winter and spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you are telling me when you use the term you are not referring to any one specific document; is that right? You are referring to a series of discussions and a series of documents related to those discussions?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a series of documents as important as this one but I didn't want to include them all. The others are mentioned in footnotes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in your report at page 6 of the English, paragraph 10, you have a list of a whole series of documents and I would suggest to you that some people who testified here in referring to the Cutileiro Plan seem to place special emphasis on the document you have listed as from the 18th of March, 1992, the text of the statement on principles for the new constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the most important document from that process from the talks and there is also the joint statement of the foreign ministers that I also cite here as a document of the international community, and one of the footnotes in my report certainly refers to that document. And specifically with regard to Bosnia-Herzegovina, the meetings held in March of 1992 are the most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the 18th March, 1992, document was really a statement about principles for further discussions about Bosnia, is that one that you say was signed by Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my request is not to require me to give general answers. I cannot know by heart everything I wrote in this report and cross-reference everything to as sources, so if you could direct me to a specific portion of my report, that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall a specific portion of your report where you make mention of what document it was that people were upset about Mr. Izetbegovic basically withdrawing his signature from, in effect. You know what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are talking about when you say that people were upset, but in footnote 145 of my expert report that is -- that refers to paragraph 121 is the one where I speak about the document from 18 March, and a dozen or so paragraphs before that speak about these efforts of the international community. But it's specifically footnote 145 which is a footnote to paragraph 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Be that as it may, if we assume that Mr. Izetbegovic had initially agreed to that document on the 18th of March, isn't it true by at least as early as the 27th of March, it was public knowledge that Mr. Izetbegovic and the SDA had withdrawn from that and publicly indicated that they were not going to be implementing the so-called Sarajevo agreement in connection with that statement of principles in relation to the Cutileiro Plan? That was well known by the 27th of March, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did it unilaterally. The process actually continued. The fact that they withdrew cannot serve as an excuse for -- with regard to the fact that they signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Right. And some individuals in the MUP, some Serb personnel felt that the proposed split should go ahead anyway in spite of the fact that Mr. Izetbegovic and the SDA had withdrawn; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. When do you say that what we call the RS MUP first came into being? What was the date of its creation, the first day it came into being?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: De jure the Law on Internal Affairs, as we know, was adopted in March and entered into force on the 31st of March, 1992. If we were to view it from a factual perspective, the collegium of the MUP issued an instruction about reporting and information. It was from April 1992 and it goes to all three sides because the collegium was composed of all three sides. It speaks about the Cutileiro Plan and the centralisation of the MUP, the story about the funding of the future ministry and so on stems from that time. That collegium meeting was attending by the closest co-workers of Alija Delimustafic and the other SDA personnel who were privy to everything and that, to my mind, would be the cut-off date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you seen a video that was shown during the Defence's opening statement in this case of Mr. Mico Stanisic in Sokolac, according to the video, on the 30th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not watch the opening statement or whatever it is called. I didn't follow it directly. I don't have time to watch that every day. I have commitments of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So I take it you are not aware that in that video dated the 30th of March, Mr. Stanisic said from today, 30th of March, they had their own MUP, meaning what would turn out later to be the RS MUP? You haven't seen that, you didn't know about it, you weren't provided that by the Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would it be a problem to watch the video now so that I could give my comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, my question is just whether you've seen it or not before?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't mind you seeing it, but actually it's close to time for the break and I ask if we could recess a couple of minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, before I resume talking about Cutileiro and 31st of March, 1st of April time-period, there are two other topics I wanted to mention. I can't remember if it was Judge Harhoff had asked you a question about what was the importance of Sokolac, and in relation to that and I wanted to ask you, do you know what the acronym SDK stands for in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is public accounting service?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, that's right. Sorry about that, yes. But I'm not an economist. I'm not very knowledgeable, well, yes, that is what it meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is it the fact that the SDK was located in Sokolac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me that was irrelevant. I cannot remember that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what the SDK did? Is that not the agency or the organ that was in control of paying out public monies including salaries for police and the army in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be that, but I really do not know about these economic processes that were developing, especially not financial ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am terribly sorry, there is -- I'm experiencing a problem with my LiveNote because so far pages had 25 lines, now I'm at line 46 of this particular page, so I don't know if that will create a problem in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That may be the latest attempt to cut down the number of pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I was having the same problem but I see now that we are on a new page. We'll see how many lines we have on this one, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Professor, the other topic I wanted to ask before returning to the 31st of March was to ask you a couple of questions about the Law on All People's Defence. First of all, the SRBiH Law on All People's Defence, this in the law library is L26 and it's Article 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure we have an English translation in e-court for that portion of the law but maybe I can just ask the witness to read out from the Serbian and if we can go to page B16 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you in particular about Article 107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Why did I assume that everything in the law library had been translated, that it was a condition of inclusion that it had been already translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That was the same assumption I was under, Your Honour, until I went to look for this particular thing and I guess that requires further inspection to see if it's only this one or if there are others. I thought that was the agreed plan that we were all trying to work from. We do have a translation which we can provide and get in e-court but I want to make sure we have the whole document translated. However, with your leave, Your Honours, may I proceed with this one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have page 16 of the B/C/S on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, Article 107. You see that? Could you read it out for us to make sure we get a proper English.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 107 reads as follows: "The Presidency of the SRBiH, in accordance with the decision of the Presidency of the SFRY from Article 105 of the federal law, hereby orders the use of units of the Territorial Defence for carrying out tasks related to public law and order and carrying out other tasks related to social self-protection. While carrying out the tasks referred to in Article 105, paragraph 1 of the federal law, units of the Territorial Defence shall be subordinated to the appropriate organ of the interior."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not this provision was ever in effect in Bosnia in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia? That is too broad for me. I haven't found a specific document about that and I'm not commenting upon this Article 107 in that context if I did provide a comment on this article. I would like to see the paragraph in which I provide a comment on this article and in which context.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know if you do. Perhaps Mr. Zecevic on redirect may point you to it if there is one. But we see reference here to the federal law and if we can look at that, I'd ask you to speak to that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from e-court that's L001 from the law library at page 18 of the B/C/S and page 67 of the English. I believe we'll find Article 105 of the federal law of the SFRY law.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you have that in front of you now, Professor?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It talks about: "In the event of an immediate threat of war and other emergencies, the task of maintaining public law and order and other tasks pertaining to social self-protection may be carried out by Territorial Defence units." Were you familiar with this provision of the federal law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't see what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see no problem. Would you agree with me that this seems to provide for the possibility that the TO could be used to carry out certain tasks that were traditionally in the remit of the police of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in accordance with the decision of the Presidency of the SFRY as stated in the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question before returning to 31 March, it's related -- you've talked about in Annex 9 Exhibit 1D78 which purports to refer to a MUP collegium meeting on the 1st of April, 1992, and in connection with that in your report at footnote 148 you make reference to the testimony of Mr. Delimustafic and Mr. Mandic's state court proceedings. Apparently to support the proposition that this so-called instruction on reporting, as you call it, was all part of the Cutileiro Plan to peacefully split the MUP and that apparently this is confirmed. Are you saying it's confirmed by Mr. Delimustafic in his state court testimony? Is that why you put it in the footnote?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to it as one of the confirmations provided by one of the participants in the event. It is the instruction of the 1st of April that is true confirmation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But can you direct me to a page and a line number in Mr. Delimustafic's transcript where he says that there was such a collegium meeting on the 1st of April and that he knew about it and that he was in agreement with the so-called peaceful split?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if my memory serves me well, Mr. Hannis objected when I tried to use the document with the witness and I was actually prohibited for using the document with the witness during my direct examination based on the objection which Mr. Hannis is doing. Now, I was -- based on his objection. And I'm perfectly fine with Mr. Hannis using this document because I want to rely on that document, as I stated during my direct, but I think only proper way would be that the document is shown to the witness so he can comment on it. I can give you the reference if you bear with me for just one second. It's a tab number in our announced documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I'm trying to avoid is letting Mr. Zecevic get into the back door what I'm trying to keep out completely. However, what I'm doing here is I'm trying to go to another example, the witness's reliance on something to support a point when the source document, I say, does not prove that point. Now, this is a bit of a dilemma for me because in order to do that somebody has to look at the document and say there's no reference in here by Mr. Delimustafic saying that he was aware of that or he agreed to it or anything to that effect. Now, if Trial Chamber is going to take the position that if I want to pursue that then the whole document comes in then I withdraw the question because I think there is no proper way for that testimony by Mr. Delimustafic in state court to come into evidence in this court without Mr. Delimustafic coming here and testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A couple of matters, Your Honours. First, it's tab 33 for the reference of Mr. Hannis if he wants to use it at the end of the day. The second thing, I don't think it's -- maybe the witness should be excused while we are discussing these matters. And the third thing, according to the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, the hearsay evidence is permitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, it appears to us that the problems created by the course which you have explained you seek to follow are -- I don't want to use the word insurmountable but present their own difficulties and the preferable course would be to withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll do that, Your Honour. Withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Professor, I want to go now back to what we started to talk about before the break and that was the events around the 31st of March and the 1st of April concerning the -- what I call the joint MUP that was still in existence at that time. I think you are familiar with a dispatch that was sent out by Momo Mandic on the 31st of March; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were several dispatches on those days, but, again, I you would like a reference to a paragraph and a footnote where I cite the document. It will be easier for me to answer the question that may follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm checking, Professor, to see if you actually cite it in your report. I believe it's in footnote 205?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And for the record, this is Exhibit P353. If we could have that up in e-court, please. I see it's page 69 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Professor, I'm sorry, for you it appears to be on page 59 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, it's on your screen. Having taken a look at that does that refresh your memory about what that dispatch was about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, for easy reference is that tab number 14 in your list?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know. I don't have my list in front of me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Smith should know, shouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Isn't that Mr. Mandic telling everyone that we are forming our Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among other things he also speaks about that in this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you will see at the top that has a dispatch number 02-2482 and there's a fax header line which it looks like this was sent on the 31st of March at 1358 hours, 1.58 in the afternoon, by fax. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's very small. Yes, now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And it looks like it went from the MUP to Radio SA, I think that's Radio Sarajevo, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I can see it says MUP BiH Sarajevo, that's enough for me, which means that it was sent from the MUP headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now are you aware that one minute later on that same date there was a dispatch sent by Delimustafic basically disagree with what Mr. Mandic sends in this one? Have you seen that document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both were high-ranking officials of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. What is there for me to assess there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, no, I'm asking you if you saw a different dispatch sent by the minister, Mr. Delimustafic, who was Mr. Mandic's boss at the time still sent one minute later according to the fax header by Mr. Delimustafic basically disavowing what Mr. Mandic is calling for here? Have you seen that document? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that other document is my footnote number 206, isn't it? That follows from the context of paragraph 169.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Professor, I'm sorry. Your footnote 206 is a dispatch by Delimustafic, but on the 10th of April -- and that is not the same one that I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, the one I'm talking about is 1D136 which is not on my list of documents to be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But, Professor, absent leave of the Court or agreement from my learned friends across the way, I can't show it to you, but I'm asking you if you refer -- if you recall seeing a document sent the same day, 31st of March, by Delimustafic following up Mr. Mandic's dispatch and disagreeing with it basically? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot speak from memory. I would like to see the document and it would be no problem for me to comment then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm in your hands. I did not have it on the list but given the witness's request and it is a document in evidence, I would ask that he be shown 1D136.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, Professor, we'll bring that up on the screen for you. And take your time to read it and let me know when you've finished.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Had you seen it before today before reading it just now? Had you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I have. Now I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you didn't cite this one in your report, did you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can comment this document if necessary but then I would need a couple of minutes to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, but my question for the moment is: You did not cite this one in your report, did you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this paragraph. Maybe elsewhere, but even if I haven't, I have a position or an opinion about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, what is that opinion, other than your apparent opinion that it wasn't worthy of including in your report?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say right away, I said that on those days several very interesting dispatches were sent out from the MUP. On the following day, the collegium meeting took place with all the highest-ranking officials of which only Alija Delimustafic was missing, only he was absent. And all the MUP officials that were delegated by the three ruling parties agree with the contents of the dispatch of the 1st of April. This to my mind speaks about the very bad relations between these two gentlemen, although one is minister and the other assistant minister. And some allegations here concerning the MUP of the Socialist Republic of BH are false because a year earlier Mr. Alija Delimustafic acted very differently toward the MUP of the Socialist Republic of BH, very different from what he says here. He accepted the fact that only SDA personnel went or attended training in Croatia for months, although there is a training centre at Vraca just outside Sarajevo where MUP members had been trained for decades. Half of this dispatch to me looks like mere sermon ising.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, under your understanding of the Law on Internal Affairs and the rules, what is the appropriateness of Mr. Mandic as assistant minister sending out the dispatch he sent out a minute earlier than this one? Any provision in the then existing rules or Law on Internal Affairs to do that? Seems like Mr. Delimustafic would be appropriate to be upset and sermonising about that.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot go into the relations between the minister and his assistant and who sent what kind of dispatch at what minute exactly, but I could ask myself how the assistant can send out something and a minute later the minister disavows it. This really wasn't something that I analysed deeply.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, but in your direct examination by Mr. Zecevic when you were talking about the 1 April dispatch that you referred to as the instruction on reporting, which you say shows the collegium, apart from Mr. Delimustafic, had agreed to this split, you said one of the reasons that you found that document to be reliable was the fact that Mr. Delimustafic apparently didn't make any complaint about it until the 10th of April, which is that other document you told me about in your footnote 206, I think. 1D138. But you didn't mention this document that sent the very same day where he is complaining about it. Don't you think that's a significant omission on your part when you are reaching the conclusion that Delimustafic didn't have a problem with what was happening on the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't call this document instruction on reporting. That's his official name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying you called this document that. I'm saying you called 1D78, the 1 April collegium document, which you put in as your Annex 9, is the one that you call instruction on reporting; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I continue with my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this analysis, I didn't deal with Alija Delimustafic as minister of the interior and each and every one of his dispatches, but considering the whole I wrote my report and the specific things that are linked to this document. I said that I saw a great many documents but only cited part of them in my footnotes. If I did not comment on this document in my report, well, then you have my opinion that I stated orally a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Then let me show you another document that appears to be related to all this. It's 65 ter number 20060.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this was on my list at tab 16. If we could have that up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, while it's coming up, I will tell you that this actually appears to be within this document three separate dispatches. The first one you'll see is dated the 1st of April, 1992, and it's to all the CSBs and the SJBs, police administrations and all the administrations at headquarters. It says: "Due to the occurrence of a certain number of employees being absent from work for various reasons, this in some organisational units and in particular after UZSK, the crime prevention administration dispatch number 02-2482 of 31/03/1992," and you may recall that's the number of Mr. Momcilo Mandic's dispatch on the 31st that we looked at a few minutes ago, "in the view of the overall security situation in the republic, the professional collegium requires heads of all organisational units and renders them responsible for the creation of normal working conditions ..." And you'll see 1, 2, 3 -- 13 names, I believe, and 12 signatures. Would you agree those persons named are the high-ranking members of the MUP who would be part of the professional collegium of the MUP at that time?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were high-ranking officials in the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it appears that we have signatures by all the names except the name of Mico Stanisic? You see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It seems to me that this is sort of the appropriate format for a dispatch purported to be coming from the collegium to go out? By that, I mean it has the names of everyone and it has the signatures. Wouldn't that lead you to conclude that this is an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a singular dispatch. This is the first time I see something like this in my life. This is the first time I see everyone who participated signing it. This is a singular example of everyone who attended a meeting signing the document that ensued and my association leads me elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, given the particular circumstances of the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in particular in the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time, does it seem inappropriate to you that this might be an event where it was deemed that this was indeed a moment to have all the names and signatures attached because it was a critical moment in time for that MUP, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these were very important moments for the ministry, but, as I'm saying, this is a singular dispatch. I'm now expressing my doubt and saying that never did another dispatch leave the ministry with everybody's signatures on it. That is a singular case that all the participants in a collegium meeting signed this. Usually it's the minister who signs it or his deputy or one of the assistants or somebody who the minister authorises, but for everyone to sign it, this is a singular document as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, now you are an expert on communications, are you telling us -- you started to work for the MUP in April of 1992 so before this date you hadn't even worked at MUP, do you know how the dispatches went out from the BiH MUP prior to 1992? How many collegium documents have you looked at from that MUP before 1 April 1992? 10, 100, 1.000? What do you base your opinion on?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you know, this is the second time I am appearing before this Honourable Court. What I saw from the period of the functioning of the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I never saw any document of any kind that was signed by all the participants, usually it is the person chairing the collegium meeting that signs such a document. I'm not going to guess now whether I saw 3, 5, 7 or 57 documents of that kind, however, everything I saw, all the documents leaving the ministry, I never saw any document that was signed by all the participants involved, say all the participants in a particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to annex number 9 to your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I do that, Your Honours, I'd like to tender 20060.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I was just -- you see that this document has a 65 ter number 20.000 something, so it's not on the original list of the 65 ter documents for the Office of the Prosecutor. This document we received it when it was announced by Mr. Hannis. Now, Mr. Hannis was criticising me at the very beginning for not showing the documents to some of the witnesses and I explained that we didn't have the document. This document did not appear before in this trial and we had Vitomir Zepinic, we had Momcilo Mandic and we had even the OTP expert here, Professor Nielsen, and this document never surfaced before. Now, this is the document that we received after this witness has been -- has started his testimony. We haven't been disclosed this document before. The Office of the Prosecutor has not put it on its original 65 ter list. It bears the name of Mr. Mico Stanisic and if this document was -- was as it appears to be, it should have been disclosed to the Defence much earlier, therefore, I do object admitting this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First of all, it does bear the name of Mr. Stanisic but not the signature. We weren't required to provide the Defence every document that had Mr. Stanisic's name on it. That could be any newspaper article since 1990. Your Honour, I don't know why we didn't find it sooner but it does appear to be authentic on its face, and the other arguments, I say, should go to weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness have not seen this document of course because we never had it in our possession before. Now, I don't see any basis for introducing this document through this witness because the witness haven't seen this document nor does he comment on that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, do I understand you to say that you just recently discovered this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure we've had it in our possession for a long time. I only recently discovered it. I don't know how long it's been in the collection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do you agree that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears that it's been in the collection for ten years or more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the face of it, it should have been disclosed during your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I would have wanted to use it with Christian Nielsen when he testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt, Your Honours, but my Case Manager has brought to my attention that apparently we did disclose it to the Defence in October of 2009. I can't jump up and down too much about that because I didn't discover it myself but it has been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In the interests of time, because of the issues that this raises, we would mark it for identification at this stage. Pending the outcome of -- there's a live issue before us about Rule 66 which we expect to deliver in the course of this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P2320 MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Professor, I did want to talk about your Annex 9 which is footnoted as Exhibit -- well, it's 1D78 is the exhibit. It's the 1 April 1992 dispatch which you have captioned as "Instructions on reporting." Do you have your copy in your report in front of you, Professor? Do you have the hard copy of yours?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have annex number 9 in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we have on the screen 1D78, the copy of that dispatch and I want to ask you some questions. On this original, I don't see anywhere where it says "instructions on reporting," so that term, as appears twice in your Annex 9, is something that you've added; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what that document is called.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where is it called? Not in the document itself? Where do you say --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, instructions on reporting, dispatch, it doesn't matter. I typed out the original of the text here and that's what matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem -- go ahead. You had something more?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was it. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But, Professor, I disagree. I think it does matter. You've said you picked out these documents for your annexes because they were the most important and you've included in your annex something that is not in the original document. Don't you see a problem with that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I entitled it because some other documents also refer to this document and they say instructions on reporting, but the important thing is that I conveyed or retyped this dispatch as is stated in the original which we see in e-court on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But, Professor, you did not type it as in accordance with the original because you have several differences. You've added things, you've changed things, and you've left things out, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the MUP of the SRBiH up until the end where the inverted commas are, I think that I typed it all out correctly and what I wanted to point out I did, right, and that is why I put it in the annex. I highlighted what it was that I wanted to highlight in that annex in capital letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, that's another thing. In your Annex 9, it appears that you have underlined and put in bold parts of the original that are not underlined and in bold in the original; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I did that so that every reader could be guided to the key sentence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you see the original of 1D78 on the page in front of you. Immediately under line 1 that says MUP SRBiH, there's a dispatch number. What does it say after the dispatch number in the original? It's a word that looks like "sluzbeno"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: DD, that's the mark of the dispatch, that is how it's sent through this information system, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, look at line 2. Dispatch number. What is the word after dispatch number in line 2 of the original on the screen? It's not --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the number, then one I see here P0044293, so I refer to that number too. I mean, if it's on the document why do you have a problem with me putting it there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, what is the word immediately following the word "broj" and the colon in line 2? Isn't that the Serbian word that means "official"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "sluzbeno" means official.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you don't have the official in your Annex 9. Instead you've put in a seven digit number, 0044293; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you see that is the number that I conveyed from the original document. I didn't want to create any confusion there. You see that it says P and then the numbers follows; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Professor, and having looked at a lot of the documents from the OTP, are you not aware that that number is an ERN, an evidence record number, an interior number used by the OTP to stamp their documents? You didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's what I often wrote in my footnotes, and you will see in many footnotes these numbers are in brackets simply to make things easier for those who are going to prepare the report for further publication. I always use these numbers. In many footnotes you have these numbers that I found this way on documents. You can have a look and we can have a look, we'll see many such cases. In footnotes such numbers are placed in brackets. It was my attempt to help someone from the Defence team who will be dealing with these reports to find those documents more easily. There's no other reason for those numbers to be there. For those reasons I placed those documents there, and I just need a bit of time and I can find it in many other sources. I mean, in many other footnotes. For example, footnote 218, the same thing, again this number is in parentheses and in bold.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine to cite it in a footnote as a source, but you put that number in the place where one would expect to see a number because dispatches typically have numbers; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I have done my utmost to understand you as well as I can while you were asking your last few questions. I copied the number from the original document, even if it is a technical error, I don't see whether that changes anything essential in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it has to do with your level of professionalism, I would say, and you've omitted the word "official," that's disappeared, and now you've stuck the last seven digits of the that ERN into the place where "official" appeared. But let's go on to something that's maybe more substantive. In the first paragraph in the original on the screen, can you go down in the first paragraph, the seventh line that in B/C/S appears to have the words "Republika Srpskog," you see that? You find that, Professor?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And following on from that, after the word BiH, there's a comma and a new phrase that starts with the word "stupio," s-t-u-p-i-o, and it appears to me with the help from my language assistant that beginning from that word to the next comma, that phrase has been omitted from what you typed up and put in Annex 9; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My Annex 9 is the processed version of this document. There's the original and there's this. But the essence of the original document is not disrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, at best, at best it's very negligent and possibly more than that, but at least misleading, the way you've described what you did with your annexes you told us you pick out those documents because they were important, you put this one in your annex, it has a quotation mark around it leading one to believe that that is a correct, accurate quote from the original. Don't you see that as a problem?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see it as a problem if I have the original document. I haven't made up anything in the annex, anything that's essential in this document. That's why there is a footnote that shows how exactly it is put here, and apart from that, Annex 12 isn't part of my footnotes either. It's a separate annex. There's the original document and we can discuss it without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Professor, you are a teacher, what kind of grade would you give one of your students who submitted a report like this with all the various kinds of mistakes and errors we pointed out?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are technical mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here you go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I was caught by surprise that Mr. Hannis would finish so early because the last break he informed me that he might be finishing today. If with the leave of the Trial Chamber, I would like to have redirect examination tomorrow morning if I may, perhaps 20 minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And your next witness is to follow immediately after, isn't it? I haven't read your most recent e-mail since our discussion on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, Professor Pasalic is our next expert witness and he is ready to start probably tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment to tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.
